description: m_n = m_p·(1+X/(1-X/2)) wrapper analysis. Verifies the wrapper is an exact algebraic identity; demonstrates the residual is intrinsic to X(q); cross-anchor sensitivity argument for the 100× target reachability.

data.verdict:
WRAPPER IS EXACT ALGEBRAIC IDENTITY — m_n = m_p·(1+X/2)/(1-X/2) equals m_p·(1+X/(1-X/2)) to compute precision. The wrapper does NOT contribute residual; the 0.10% intrinsic X(q) residual propagates to ~1 ppm m_n residual (consistent with observed 2 ppm m_n miss).

100× TARGET REACHABILITY: 1 ppb m_n needs ΔX/X precision of 725.97 ppb. Cross-anchor (q_p ↔ q_m) gives ΔX/X = 321.9 ppb — a 0× INSUFFICIENT signal to discriminate Habiro candidates at the 100× target precision. This explains PR #1675 Item 2's universal TIER 2 verdict: all candidates landed at the SAME residual because cross-anchor can't see the required structure.

PATH FORWARD: (a) third q_0 anchor with larger Δq, or (b) algebraic-derivation Habiro element from first principles (not numerical fit), or (c) higher-precision q_proton observable for finer Habiro discrimination.
data.path_forward: (a) third q_0 anchor with larger Δq for triangulation, (b) algebraic-derivation Habiro element (not numerical fit), (c) higher-precision q_proton observable for finer Habiro discrimination.
